messages:
alex: Heads-up: after last Vault rotation (yesterday evening) prod saw a burst of secret churn in payments namespaces. K8s events show ExternalSecrets controller repeatedly updating Secrets.
maria: Are values changing or just metadata/annotations?
alex: Mostly metadata diffs — kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration and one of our deploy annotations toggling. Kube-apiserver logs show many small updates.
jonathan: Which ExternalSecrets operator version? Can you paste a couple events?
alex: operator v0.5.3. Event snippet:
```
Normal Reconcile external-secrets/payments-db  ExternalSecret synced, created Secret payments/db-creds
Normal Update   secret/payments-db   Updated by external-secrets-controller (metadata changed)
Normal Reconcile external-secrets/payments-db  ExternalSecret synced, patching Secret (metadata)
```
maria: That looks like something else is mutating the Secret after ES writes it (deploy hook or sidecar). If metadata flips, ES will keep reconciling.
jonathan: We had this before with the post-deploy job reapplying manifests which rewrites last-applied. @nina any deploy hooks that touch live Secrets?
nina: Not intentionally — pipeline only applies kustomize overlays. But I found a recent TF change that added `kubectl apply --prune` in the post-deploy step. Checking CI logs now.
infra-bot: Deploy job #4821 for payments-service succeeded (2024-04-06T21:34:12Z)
alex: Two mitigation paths: stop re-applying Secrets from deploys, or make ES create Secrets with stable metadata so it doesn't fight. Also we can slow ES resync.
maria: Quick mitigations: 1) Bump controller resync interval so ES isn't aggressive. 2) Patch Helm values via Terraform to set controller extraArgs/resync-interval.
jonathan: Terraform snippet to override helm_release values:
```
set {
  name  = "controller.extraArgs.resync-interval"
  value = "5m"
}
```
jonathan: That should reduce thundering when external actors briefly touch Secrets.
alex: Also stop the deploy pipeline from reapplying live Secrets (or switch to server-side apply). Short-term, adding a fixed annotation set in ExternalSecret target.template.metadata could make ES writes stable.
maria: ExternalSecrets supports target.template.metadata. We can add a stable annotation like `secrets.redwood.com/managed-by: external-secrets` so it doesn't include transient last-applied.
jonathan: Example ExternalSecret patch for kustomize overlay:
```
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: payments-db
spec:
  target:
    name: payments-db
    template:
      metadata:
        annotations:
          secrets.redwood.com/managed-by: external-secrets
```

nina: CI logs confirm the `kubectl apply --prune` addition in infra-pipeline TF overlay (recent commit). I'll open a revert PR for the post-deploy apply and add a note to stop applying Secrets.
alex: Action items: 1) jonathan — open TF PR to set ES resync-interval to 5m (helm values). 2) nina — revert prune/apply in pipeline and add ticket to avoid applying Secrets. If both done we should see churn stop.
jonathan: PR posted: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/terraform/merge_requests/1234 — merged to staging, will roll to prod after smokecheck.
maria: Also propose a small alert/probe: detect >5 Secret updates/hour in a namespace and page SRE-oncall.
alex: I'll sketch an alert and add to runbook. If churn persists after these changes we'll inspect ownerReferences and consider preserveOnDelete or resourcePolicy tweaks.
sre-oncall: On it — will pause deploys if we see a surge and page infra.
maria: If anyone gets repro steps (short script/config) drop them here so we can reproduce in staging.
